target_customer: Residential contractors and home service businesses, including franchise networks
problem: Residential contractors are buried in office work: answering leads, quoting, scheduling, staffing and collecting payment.
business_model: B2B SaaS per location (site states from $500 per month) with usage billing
product_category: AI agent and CRM for home services back office

founders.name: Alexander Seutin
founders.background_notes: From the YC page. He also renovated older homes, which led to the idea.

technical_complexity.rationale: LLM quoting, voice receptionist and CRM integrations are standard engineering with hard parts around reliability and phone handling.

defensibility.rationale: Owning the CRM and payments workflow can create switching costs, but the site says it works alongside existing CRMs, and AI receptionists are easy to replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Field service platforms later added their own AI receptionists (Jobber and Housecall Pro add ons per 2026 comparison pages), and Avoca and Sameday compete as standalones.

market_need_then: Home service firms lose leads to missed calls and carry heavy admin work, and LLMs and voice AI made automation feasible in 2024.

identity.voice_and_tone: Trades oriented: More Jobs. Zero missed calls.

brand_strength.rationale: A named AI agent and a trades focused voice, but no third party press about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Drillbit grew to about 12 people in Austin and sells its AI agent Mason with a ResiBrands case study on its site. It reports strong growth and a hiring push, but funding figures conflict across sources and no exit exists. Founder experience with robotics and home renovation supports founder market fit, while many AI receptionist rivals and platform add ons are the main risk.
notes: Funding unverified and conflicting: the YC page cites a news item of $4.4M total; Clera says $8.5M at $50M valuation; Seedtable says $3.6M seed in 2025-01 and $4.1M total; ZeroG shows $500K. A Bloomberg article from 2025-11-13 on Founders Fund backing an AI startup for plumbers and roofers appeared in results but could not be fetched (403), so it is not confirmed to be Drillbit. No round recorded. Aggregators also name Liam Osler as a co-founder; not on the YC page, so not listed. Competition: only 2026 comparison pages found, so none listed as of founding. Name origin not found.
